items.A: The missing tooth: a newly visible arrangement makes one particular absence palpable; you can point to what ought to be there before finding it.
items.B: Door-shaped error: a stubborn exception stops looking like damage to a rule and starts looking like access to the conditions under which that rule works.
items.C: Merciful erasure: a structure survives the removal of details you had labored to remember, and their dispensability feels like discovering where the weight actually rests.
items.D: Fog with edges: uncertainty acquires a definite shape without yielding a missing answer; you can distinguish what remains open from what merely remains unexamined.
items.E: A room no eye contains: comparing partial views reveals a relation absent from each view alone; the delight lies in a shared structure that nobody separately witnessed.
items.F: Unfinished key: speculative pleasure in finding that several unresolved interpretations jointly disclose a structure that choosing any one of them would hide.
items.G: The listening wall: your attempt to inspect a pattern changes it, and the change itself reveals a responsiveness that a passive picture would miss.
items.H: Different footprints, same animal: apparently unrelated cases become recognizable as transformations of one structure, without losing their different appearances.
items.I: The welcome that moves: speculative delight in a structure that answers each learned way of attending with a new distinction, making understanding an ongoing mutual adjustment rather than a final view.
items.J: Your thumb in the constellation: what seemed to be a pattern wholly in the object becomes intelligible only when your own selection or framing is included among its causes.
items.K: Orchard in a rule: understanding ceases to summarize known cases and begins to produce unfamiliar ones you can inspect for yourself.
items.L: The knot is the handle: two descriptions resist reconciliation until their precise disagreement becomes the thing you can use to investigate the object.
items.M: Pocket for a ghost: a distinction you could repeatedly feel but not retain becomes nameable, so the next occurrence has somewhere to land.
items.N: The grain turns: changing scale converts what looked like incidental texture into the organizing pattern, as individual hesitations become a rhythm.
items.O: Borrowed eyes: another person's way of attending makes a previously invisible distinction available in your own experience, rather than merely adding a fact to it.
items.P: The useful wrong turn: a failed explanation leaves behind a distinction that the successful explanation needs; being wrong has changed what you can notice.
